question: Actions of cholecystokinin include which one of the following?

options.opb: Secretion of pancreatic juice rich in enzymes

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Cholecystokinin released" -> "stimulates gallbladder contraction" -> "bile release into the intestine" -> "facilitates fat digestion" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Cholecystokinin released" -> "stimulates pancreatic acinar cells" -> "secretion of pancreatic juice rich in enzymes" -> "enhances digestion of nutrients" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Cholecystokinin released" -> "increases secretion of enterokinase" -> "activates trypsinogen to trypsin" -> "enhances protein digestion" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Cholecystokinin has multiple actions" -> "includes gallbladder contraction" -> "includes secretion of pancreatic juice" -> "includes secretion of enterokinase" -> "therefore, all actions are correct" -> 92%
analysis: Cholecystokinin (CCK) is a hormone that is primarily involved in the digestive process. It is released in response to the presence of fats and proteins in the small intestine. The core actions of CCK include stimulating the contraction of the gallbladder, which releases bile into the intestine, and promoting the secretion of pancreatic juice that is rich in digestive enzymes. Additionally, CCK also increases the secretion of enterokinase, which is important for activating trypsinogen to trypsin, further aiding in protein digestion. Given that all the options presented (gallbladder contraction, pancreatic enzyme secretion, and increased enterokinase secretion) are actions attributed to CCK, the most comprehensive and correct answer is 'All'. Therefore, the best-supported option is 'All'.
